findings.title: Materials' 58-point lens gap signals earnings cliff
findings.body: Materials trades at a 53 percent compression from trailing to forward multiple, the widest in the table, with a 58-point percentile gap. The market is pricing 112 percent earnings growth next year — an extraordinary assumption for a sector whose trailing earnings are already at the 85th percentile of its five-year range.

findings.title: Utilities' forward multiple ignores flat earnings
findings.body: Utilities' forward P/E sits at the 22nd percentile while its trailing multiple is at the 2nd — a 21-point gap despite only 6 percent implied growth. The forward lens is barely cheaper than trailing, meaning analysts see almost no earnings recovery, yet the percentile gap suggests the market is treating this as a re-rating rather than a trough.

findings.title: Information Technology's forward percentile collapse outruns multiple
findings.body: IT's forward P/E percentile fell 23 points in a month to 0, the cheapest in five years, while the forward multiple itself is 18.07. The trailing lens sits at the 19th percentile, so the forward collapse is not a broad de-rating — it is a sharp bet on 61 percent earnings growth that has not yet shown up in reported numbers.
